runs.text:
Arr, shipmate, four score and seven years past, our fathers did launch upon this continent a new nation, charted in Liberty, and set upon the proposition that all men be created equal.

Now be we engaged in a great civil war, testin' whether that nation, or any nation so charted and so set, can long weather the tide. We be met upon a great battlefield of that war, come to give over a stretch of that ground as a final berth for those who here gave their lives that the nation might sail on. 'Tis fittin' and proper we do so.

But in a larger sense, we cannot dedicate this ground -- we cannot consecrate it -- we cannot hallow it. The brave crew, livin' and dead, who fought here, have consecrated it far beyond our poor power to add or take away. The world'll take little note, nor long remember what be said here, but it can never forget what they did here. It be for us, the livin', to hold fast to the unfinished work them who fought here have so nobly carried forward. It be for us to set our own helm toward the great task before us -- that from these honored dead we take on more devotion to the cause for which they gave their last full measure -- that we here highly resolve these dead shall not have gone down in vain -- that this nation, under God, shall know a new birth of freedom -- and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth, aye, shall sail on forevermore.
